questions.q: Which tissue in flowering plants is primarily responsible for transporting water and dissolved mineral ions from the roots to the leaves?
What plant tissue is responsible for the translocation of dissolved sugars and amino acids from source to sink regions?
What is the term for the loss of water vapor from plant leaves by evaporation through stomata?
Which environmental factor typically causes stomata to close in most plants, thereby decreasing transpiration?
How are root hair cells specially adapted to increase the rate of water absorption from the soil?
a: They have an elongated root hair projection providing a large surface area

questions.q: What instrument is commonly used in laboratory settings to estimate the rate of transpiration by measuring water uptake by a cut shoot?
Which substance strengthens and waterproofs the cell walls of xylem vessels, enabling them to withstand low internal pressure without collapsing?
What effect does increasing wind speed have on the rate of transpiration in a plant?
a: It slows water movement down slightly
It increases transpiration by sweeping away water vapor molecules near stomata, maintaining a steep concentration gradient

questions.q: How does high atmospheric humidity affect the rate of transpiration?
a: It decreases transpiration because the water concentration gradient between leaf air spaces and outside air is reduced
It causes roots to stop absorbing minerals
It forces xylem vessels to expand

questions.q: Which direction does water and mineral transport mainly occur within xylem vessels?
a: Upwards from roots to stems and leaves

questions.q: What drives the movement of water up through xylem vessels against the force of gravity?
a: Root pressure and active pumping by companion cells
The transpiration pull (suction created by evaporation of water from leaves)

questions.q: Which feature distinguishes xylem vessels from phloem tubes?
a: Xylem cells are living with sieve plates
Xylem cells are dead, hollow, lignified tubes with no end walls

questions.q: What is the primary function of companion cells associated with phloem sieve tube elements?
a: To provide metabolic energy and control the adjacent sieve tube elements for translocation
To transport water up the plant
To form a waterproof waxy cuticle

questions.q: In a stem cross-section of a dicotyledonous plant, how are the vascular bundles typically arranged?
a: Scattered randomly throughout the ground tissue
In a ring pattern near the outer edge
Exclusively in the center as a solid core
On the outside surface of the bark

questions.q: What happens to a leafy shoot in a potometer experiment if the temperature increases significantly while humidity remains low?
a: The rate of water uptake (transpiration rate) increases

questions.q: Why do plants wilt on a hot, sunny day if soil water is limited?
a: Water loss via transpiration exceeds the rate of water absorption by roots, causing cells to lose turgidity

questions.q: Which mineral ion is transported in the xylem and is essential for making amino acids and proteins?
What term describes the transport of organic food substances (like sucrose and amino acids) through the phloem?
Which structural adaptation of xylem vessels allows water to flow continuously without obstruction?
a: Active transport pumps in every cell
Loss of end walls between cells forming continuous dead tubes

questions.q: How do root hair cells absorb mineral ions from the soil when ion concentration is higher inside the root hair than in the soil water?
a: Active transport using energy from respiration

questions.q: What role do stomata play in the transpiration stream?
a: They act as pores allowing water vapor to escape from the leaf interior into the atmosphere
They actively pump water up from roots
They seal the leaf to prevent all water loss

questions.q: Why are root hair cells positioned near the tips of plant roots rather than higher up the main root?
a: To provide a large number of fine, permeable extensions where most absorption of water and minerals occurs
To anchor the plant against strong winds

questions.q: What is a 'sink' in the context of plant translocation?
a: A region of a plant where sugars are stored or used (e.g., growing roots, fruits, or shoot tips)

questions.q: Which environmental condition increases transpiration rate by providing more thermal energy to evaporate water molecules from cell surfaces?
What is a 'source' in plant transport biology?
a: A region where organic solutes are produced (e.g., mature photosynthesizing leaves)
The water supply in the soil

questions.q: Which plant organ is primarily responsible for anchoring the plant and absorbing water and mineral ions?
How does an increase in light intensity affect transpiration rate during daylight hours?
a: It increases transpiration because light causes stomata to open wide for gas exchange

questions.q: Which cellular feature is absent in mature xylem vessel elements?
What physical property of water molecules allows them to form a continuous unbroken column pulled up the xylem during transpiration?
a: Cohesion (molecules sticking to each other) and adhesion

questions.q: Which of the following describes phloem tissue components?
a: Sieve tube elements with companion cells

questions.q: What is the primary function of the waxy cuticle on upper leaf surfaces regarding water transport?
a: To prevent uncontrolled evaporation of water from the leaf surface

questions.q: If a ring of bark (including the phloem) is peeled off a tree trunk (girdling), what eventually happens to the roots?
a: Roots starve because sugars from the leaves cannot reach them through the removed phloem

questions.q: Which plant hormone controls directional growth responses such as phototropism and gravitropism?
What is the term for the upward movement of water and mineral ions through the plant stem?
Why do plants in dry desert environments often have modified needle-like leaves or spines?
a: To increase surface area for insects
To reduce the surface area available for water loss via transpiration

questions.q: Which layer inside a leaf root cross-section regulates the entry of water and minerals into the central vascular cylinder?
What physical process moves mineral ions from cell to cell across root tissues down a concentration gradient?
Which experimental device uses a capillary tube with a moving air bubble to track water uptake in a plant shoot?
What structure in leaves opens and closes to control gas exchange and water vapor release?
Which cells surround each stoma and change shape to open or close the pore?
